title: BlueHorizon Health - Redwood Onboarding Kickoff
summary: Kickoff for BlueHorizon Health onboarding to Redwood Dedicated/Private stack. Covered goals, success criteria, timeline, basic architecture, security requirements (SOC 2, SSO), and first POC scope (chat triage + embeddings). Agreed next steps: share onboarding playbook and security pack, schedule infra access call, plan two-week pilot with metrics and benchmark plan.
topics: Onboarding plan: pilot scope, infra access, data flows
action_items: Sam Reyes - Share onboarding playbook + support contact (due 2027-12-24)
Liam Patel - Send infra access checklist and VPC peering doc (due 2028-01-03)
Maya Thompson - Provide sample data schema and redaction requirements (due 2027-12-29)
Priya Singh - Confirm compliance requirements and list of auditors (due 2027-12-28)
Jordan Kim - Schedule dedicated performance baseline run and propose benchmark tests (due 2028-01-06)
next_steps: Redwood to send security & SOC2 summary and KMS/HSM integration guide
Customer to provision test VPC and create infra user for Redwood SE
Plan two-week pilot focusing on chat triage model + embeddings for search
Schedule performance benchmark week and post-pilot review
transcript:
[00:00] Anna Liu: hi everyone, thanks for joining, i'm anna from redwood i'm the account lead for bluehorizon, quick around the room?
[00:10] Maya Thompson: hey i'm maya, director of ml at bluehorizon, leading this project, excited to get started
[00:15] Tom Alvarez: tom here, lead devops, i'll handle network and infra stuff
[00:20] Priya Singh: priya, security and privacy - i'll own compliance questions
[00:25] Ethan Reed: ethan, product manager, focused on timelines and success metrics
[00:30] Sam Reyes: sam from redwood cs, i'll run the onboarding playbook and help with rollout
[00:36] Liam Patel: liam, se, i'll be your technical point for benchmarks, perf and model mappings, and jordan's on the call too
[00:44] Jordan Kim: hey everyone, jordan here, solutions eng - will help with test harness and evals
[00:50] Anna Liu: great, thanks. goal for today is align on what success looks like for the first 8 weeks, confirm security posture, and get infra checklist moving. maya, can you share the top business outcomes?
[01:05] Maya Thompson: sure, two things: reduce triage time for inbound patient messages by 60% and improve our internal search relevancy by using embeddings; we want a pilot that proves latency and accuracy within production-ish traffic
[01:22] Ethan Reed: timeline wise we want a pilot in jan, 2 weeks of traffic replay, then decide on dedicated vs private in feb
[01:30] Anna Liu: that sounds reasonable. quick qual Qs - do you have existing vector db and pipeline or do you need redwood to host embeddings?
[01:40] Maya Thompson: we have an elastic-based embeddings store today, but it's a homegrown setup, may want oak to offload - sorry, i mean we'd consider redwood-managed embeddings if it simplifies ops
[01:51] Liam Patel: got it, for the pilot we can integrate with your existing store, we often do a hybrid where we push embeddings to your vector DB; we'll document patterns
[01:59] Tom Alvarez: on networking, preference is VPC/private deployment, data never leaves our account, we need peering and KMS control
[02:08] Priya Singh: also SOC two controls and audit logs are mandatory for us, plus SSO, RBAC and IDP integration, and data retention policies - minimal retention for PHI
[02:20] Sam Reyes: we support private deployments and dedicated pools; for the SOC two, we'll send the latest attestation and our compliance pack after this call
[02:28] Maya Thompson: can you confirm KMS/HSM support? we need key ownership for all customer data at rest
[02:34] Jordan Kim: yes we support customer-managed KMS in both dedicated and private modes, and we can show the integration steps. small note: sometimes the doc mentions KV cash \u2014 i always laugh, it's kv cache not cash \u2014 transcription haha
[02:47] Anna Liu: haha noted. liam, can you walk through the basic pilot architecture we propose?
[02:55] Liam Patel: sure, simple flow: app -> api gateway -> redwood router -> model pool. for private we'll deploy a control plane that talks to your VPC via peering; inference nodes stay in your network. caching: we recommend prefix caching for common prompts and TTL for embeddings; we'll check sequence lengths but expect sub-300 token avg.
[03:18] Maya Thompson: what's the latency we should expect for chat triage? under 300 ms for small prompts?
[03:25] Liam Patel: for dedicated with optimized kernels we often see 80-200ms p50 for our mid-sized models at small batch sizes, p95 depends on peak concurrency and KV cache hit rate. we'll run a baseline.
[03:38] Tom Alvarez: any special kernel or quantization compatibility we need to know about for our on-prem gpus? we run a mix of a40 and t4s
[03:46] Jordan Kim: we support several quantization profiles. a40 is great, t4 may need int8/4bit optimizations. we'll provide recommended configs; sometimes model flavor names are slightly different between repos and docs so we'll sync a model mapping sheet
[04:02] Priya Singh: on logging, we need the logging to be audit-ready; who has access to logs, how long retained, and can we mute PII from logs?
[04:12] Sam Reyes: yes, retention is configurable and we support redaction hooks. for private deployments logs can be stored in customer S3 and only metadata pointers in the control plane. we'll include an audit log design doc link in the pack (drive link shared in chat)
[04:28] Maya Thompson: great. another Q on data residency \u2014 we operate in eu-west and us-west; for PHI we need processing within region where data originates
[04:37] Anna Liu: we can regionally pin inference nodes; for private we can deploy only in your region, and for dedicated we can allocate regional pools. we'll document region placement constraints and any added latency/cost implications
[04:49] Ethan Reed: can you run a quick runbook for the pilot metrics \u2014 what do you need from us?
[04:55] Liam Patel: we want sample traffic, a replay harness, a labeled eval set for triage accuracy, and baseline cost/latency targets. we'll instrument token-level cost, p50/p95 latency, embed similarity recall, and error rates.
[05:10] Maya Thompson: we'll share a 2k message sample and our relevancy testset by next tuesday
[05:18] Tom Alvarez: infra access, we'll create an infra user and a test VPC and grant peering endpoints as per the checklist
[05:25] Priya Singh: i'll coordinate the auditors and provide a list of our compliance questions
[05:30] Anna Liu: excellent. any blockers or open concerns?
[05:35] Priya Singh: encryption at rest and in transit covered, just want to see formal attestation and the KMS flow end-to-end
[05:43] Sam Reyes: we'll send the SOC2 cert, and a KMS integration walkthrough \u2014 it's in the security pack
[05:49] Jordan Kim: we'll also include a sample benchmarking script and a colab/spreadsheet to collect results. we'll mis-transcribe some model names sometimes so we'll maintain a mapping sheet.
[06:00] Anna Liu: ok to recap: redwood to send security pack, onboarding playbook, infra checklist this week; bluehorizon to provision test VPC, share sample data and compliance list; schedule SE-led infra call next week; pilot planned for early jan.
[06:18] Maya Thompson: yep sounds good
[06:20] Ethan Reed: agree
[06:22] Tom Alvarez: i'll start the VPC prep
[06:24] Priya Singh: i'll review the compliance pack as soon as it's available
[06:28] Anna Liu: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links and calendar invites.
[06:34] Anna Liu: action items reiterated in chat and email. meeting adjourned.
[06:40] [call end]

Notes: transcript contains occasional ASR errors (e.g., "KV cash" for KV cache, "SOC two"), and some speaker labels folded for brevity. Links referenced in chat: onboarding playbook (https://redwood.example.com/onboarding-playbook), security pack (https://redwood.example.com/security-pack), infra checklist (drive.google.com/drive/fake-link).
